name: Rolling Collar
summary: Management structure: continuously roll a collar's put and call up (or down) and out to track the share price, keeping a constant percentage floor and ceiling over time.

legs.strike_rule: new put at 0.30 delta each cycle
new call solved for near-zero net cost
legs.dte_rule: same expiry as the new put

max_profit: path-dependent; each cycle's cap is reset higher when the stock rallies
max_loss: limited to the current cycle's floor plus the cumulative net debits of all rolls
breakevens: share basis + cumulative net debits per share

greeks.delta: maintained near +50 per unit by re-striking

when_to_use: Long-term holdings that must stay hedged indefinitely - a core ETF position in an automated fleet, or a concentrated legacy position.
typical_dte: roll every 30-60 days, always as a 4-leg combo
entry_rules: Trigger the roll at DTE <= 21, OR when the short call delta >= 0.60, OR when the long put delta <= 0.12 (protection has drifted too far away).
Execute as ONE 4-leg combo: close old put + close old call + open new put + open new call.
Each roll must satisfy: net cost <= 0.3% of share notional, and new call strike >= max(share basis, previous call strike).
Refuse a roll that would lower the call strike below the previous cycle's strike after a rally (that would lock in a lower cap).
management_rules: Track cumulative roll cost as a running basis adjustment; if cumulative cost exceeds 5% of notional annually, widen the collar or reduce the frequency.
Ratchet: after any 10% rally, force a roll-up so the floor rises with the position.
Do not ratchet the floor down after a decline - hold the existing floor and let it work.
exit_rules: If the 4-leg roll cannot be filled by 15:30 ET on expiration day, fall back to closing the expiring legs outright (the position becomes unhedged shares, flagged for re-hedge next session) - never carry an ITM short call into expiry to preserve a roll.
Standard extrinsic and ex-dividend guards on the expiring short call throughout.
Full exit: unwind all legs plus shares as one order.
assignment_risk: Each cycle's short call is assignable and covered. The roll execution window is the vulnerability - a single combo order eliminates it. Around dividends, roll BEFORE the ex-date rather than into it.
buying_power: Shares plus the small per-cycle net debit.
liquidity_needs: Needs consistent liquidity across many consecutive expiries; ETFs and mega-caps only.
common_mistakes: Legging the roll; ratcheting the cap downward to fund a higher floor and slowly guaranteeing underperformance; ignoring cumulative roll costs.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
